To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of xylanase and pectinase produced concurrently by a bacterial isolate Bacillus purnilus in bioscouring of flax fibres reduced the use of scouring chemicals by 30% and bleaching chemicals by 70% to obtain the same brightness, whiteness and yellowness as achieved by conventional scouring and subsequent bleaching.
a xylano-pecinolytic enzyme mixture produced by a bacterial isolate, B. pumilus, can be used to scoure the flax fiber, which reduces the consumption of scour and bleaching chemicals.

bioscouring of the flax fibers using xylano- pectinolytic enzymes resulted in 70% reduction of the consumption of scour chemicals and 30% reduction of the bleaching chemicals to achieve the same level of brightness as achieved by conventional scouring and chemical bleaching.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an eco-friendly and cost-effective process for the bioscouring of natural fibers.
the development of a novel and cost-effective approach for bioscouring of cellulosic fibers and its application in textile industry.
the production of a xylano- pectinolytic enzyme cocktail by a bacterial isolate Bacillus purnilus and its use in the bioscouring of natural fibers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this is the first study showing the use of a xylano- pectinolytic enzymes in the bioscouring of the natural fibers and the reduction in the consumption in scouring and bleached chemical in order to make this process ecofriendly and economical.
the use of bioscouring in the textile processing is a viable option to reduce the use of chemicals, which in turn will help to save the environment.
bioscouring of the flax fibers using concurrently produced xylano-pecinolytic synergistic enzymes from a bacterial isolate, Bacillus pumilis is cost effective, ecofriendly and energy saving.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the xylanase and pectinase produced by Bacillus pumillus can be utilized in the bioscouring of fibers and the pretreated fibers can be bleached by using less amount of chemicals and can also be used for the production of high strength fabrics.

the bioscouring of natural fibers can be made more cost-effective, eco-friendly, and energy-saving by using the synergism of alkalo-thermophilic cellulase-free xylanase, pectinase and protease produced by a bacterial isolate Bacillus pumnilus.
we have shown the use of xylanase and pectinase enzymes in scouring and bleached flax fiber, which is a new application of these enzymes and also a cost-effective process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bioscouring of the flax fibers using xylano- pectinolytic enzyme produced by the isolate Bacillus purnilus is cost effective and environment friendly.

the use of xylanase-pectinase synergism in scouring of flx fibers will reduce the consumption of environment polluting scouring chemicals, reduce the energy cost and also provide high tensile strength of the fibers.
the bioscouring approach can be used as a green and sustainable approach for textile processing.
